home.title: Data-driven biodiversity science for a living planet.
home.lede: Develop data-driven methods that provide insights into the distribution and dynamics of biodiversity, through integration of environmental DNA, remote sensing, and machine learning.

pillars.title: Environmental DNA
pillars.text: We are developing and applying genetic methods to detect small traces of DNA that organisms leave behind in their habitat (environmental DNA). This provides us with comprehensive biodiversity measures of the species community at a site, which even includes the large hidden diversity of species that have not yet been scientifically described (the vast majority of species!).

pillars.title: Remote sensing
pillars.text: In our computational models we apply high-resolution geographic data produced by different remote sensing techniques. Some examples are satellite images or 3D-point clouds from airborne laser-scanning. We use these data to correlate biodiversity measures with the complex biotic and abiotic environment. Our aim is to eventually be able to make biodiversity predictions for areas that lack biodiversity data, allowing the generation of biodiversity heat maps.

pillars.title: Machine learning
pillars.text: We are actively working on building state-of-the-art machine learning models to learn the complex associations of species with their environment. These models are capable to detect areas that are of high conservation value and can aid in conservation planning and selecting sites for biodiversity offsets. Further, these methods allow us to simulate the expected response of biodiversity to specific management scenarios or other factors such as climate change.

home.mission: Develop data-driven methods that provide insights into the distribution and dynamics of biodiversity, through integration of environmental DNA, remote sensing, and machine learning.
home.definition: A multidisciplinary field that brings together large-scale, multidimensional data and advanced computational methods to provide new insights about biodiversity.
home.who_we_are: One focus is to improve field- and lab-work protocols to produce more accurate biodiversity assessments using environmental DNA. The other focus of our group is to develop computational methods that utilize these data to help us better understand and manage the spatial distribution of biodiversity. Our research is interdisciplinary, including the fields of ecology, environmental genetics, geomatics, bioinformatics, data science, and machine learning. If you have a background or interest in any of these fields and care about contributing with your work towards helping biodiversity, the Biodiversity Data Lab is the place for you!

projects.title: BIOSCANN - BIOdiversity Segmentation and Classification with Artificial Neural Networks
projects.text: BIOSCANN implements a deep-learning segmentation model that integrates multiple layers of environmental data -- satellite images, airborne laser scanning, and soil information -- to identify forests of high biodiversity value in Sweden. With this approach we produce a national data product for Sweden with high-resolution biodiversity predictions.
paragraphs: BIOSCANN implements a deep-learning segmentation model that integrates multiple layers of environmental data -- satellite images, airborne laser scanning, and soil information -- to identify forests of high biodiversity value in Sweden. With this approach we produce a national data product for Sweden with high-resolution biodiversity predictions.

projects.title: High-resolution insect diversity predictions from DNA-based monitoring
projects.text: We predict the expected insect biodiversity across Sweden at 10-m resolution using models trained on DNA data gathered from Malaise traps. The models integrate biodiversity data with high-resolution environmental layers such as land cover, vegetation structure, hydrology, and climate. This jSDM-eDNA framework delivers scalable, standardized biodiversity monitoring at management-relevant spatial resolution.
paragraphs: We predict the expected insect biodiversity across Sweden at 10-m resolution using models trained on DNA data gathered from Malaise traps. The models integrate biodiversity data with high-resolution environmental layers such as land cover, vegetation structure, hydrology, and climate. This jSDM-eDNA framework delivers scalable, standardized biodiversity monitoring at management-relevant spatial resolution.

projects.title: Limits to prediction: Why global biodiversity models fail to generalize
projects.text: This project investigates the predictive accuracy of large-scale biodiversity models. Using a global dataset of 25,987 sites from 681 studies, we evaluate linear mixed models and Bayesian hierarchical models for alpha and beta diversity. The models are tested on interpolation and extrapolation capabilities, revealing clear limits to prediction.
paragraphs: This project investigates the predictive accuracy of large-scale biodiversity models. Using a global dataset of 25,987 sites from 681 studies, we evaluate linear mixed models and Bayesian hierarchical models for alpha and beta diversity. The models are tested on interpolation and extrapolation capabilities, revealing clear limits to prediction.

projects.title: Environmental Data Downloading Pipeline
projects.text: A Python package for automated environmental data retrieval in ecological modelling. The service gives users granular control over data synthesis, allowing efficient download of geospatial information from repositories including Google Earth Engine and downstream predictive modelling applications.
paragraphs: A Python package for automated environmental data retrieval in ecological modelling. methods.title: Insect traps
paragraphs: Insects are one of the most diverse and species-rich taxonomic groups, containing about half of all species that have so far been scientifically described. Insects also act as collectors of environmental DNA, because they feed from plants, fungi, and other organisms in their surroundings.
By applying Insect Malaise traps, we capture a large portion of the above-ground insect diversity, providing comprehensive DNA samples of insects as well as their gut contents and parasites.

methods.title: Soil sampling
paragraphs: When we think of biodiversity, we often think of charismatic animals and plants, but there is an immense hidden diversity below our feet in the soil. Soil core samplers reaching up to 40 cm below the surface help us access this hidden ecosystem.
These samples provide a glimpse into fungal, invertebrate, and plant species communities that can be found below the surface.

methods.title: Prescribed Burning
paragraphs: With approximately 13,000 wildfires in Spain each year and more than 100,000 hectares burned annually, wildfire prevention is a critical priority. Prescribed burning is a land-management strategy that removes dead biomass and reduces fuel continuity.
During a PhD stay in Spain, Monica Guilera Recoder participated in prescribed burns carried out by firefighters. See more fieldwork photographs in the gallery.

current.name: Tobias Andermann
current.role: Computational Biologist & Group Leader, Assistant Professor
current.bio: I am a biodiversity researcher dedicated to providing data and computational tools for combatting the global biodiversity crisis. I work at the intersection of molecular biology, spatial ecology, and machine learning, with the mission to provide a more comprehensive view on the distribution of biodiversity, including hidden diversity of inconspicuous and undescribed species through environmental DNA.

current.name: Adrian Baggstrom
current.bio: I am a PhD student focusing on biodiversity, geomatics, remote sensing and machine learning. My interest is to research the possibilities of assessing biodiversity through remote sensing techniques such as spectral imagery, lidar and synthetic aperture radar. By combining these techniques with geospatial data and deep learning, I aim to develop tools that contribute to monitoring biodiversity at different scales.

current.name: Monica Guilera Recoder
current.bio: As an ecologist focused on the study of fungal biodiversity in forest ecosystems, my goal is to discover the unknown and protect the known. My PhD research aims to optimize environmental DNA metabarcoding techniques -- in fieldwork and labwork -- to assess fungal biodiversity more efficiently and study the impact of forestry and other human disturbances on fungal diversity.

current.name: Jakob Nystrom
current.bio: The ultimate goal of my research is to provide policymakers and companies with data and tools to make better decisions for nature and biodiversity. My research focuses on quantifying natural and anthropogenic drivers of biodiversity patterns and developing causal and predictive models for biodiversity and ecosystem integrity across taxonomic and geographical scales.

current.name: Jan Borgelt
current.bio: My academic background centers on understanding environmental changes across ecosystems, giving me a broad perspective on ecological challenges. I am particularly interested in applying data science and innovative technologies to develop computational methods that address the biodiversity crisis. As part of my research stay at the Biodiversity Data Lab, I am working with eDNA insect data to understand insect taxa and diversity across space.

current.name: Vun Wen Jie (VJ)
current.bio: Biodiversity is integral to the processes that support all life on Earth. My interest is to implement a framework that allows detection and attribution of biodiversity change to drivers, strengthening the bridge between biodiversity science and policy. This postdoc position is a collaboration with the Department for Information Technology and the Biodiversity Data Lab.

current.name: Mahwash Jamy
current.bio: I am a postdoctoral researcher fascinated by the extraordinary diversity of microbes and the evolutionary processes that shaped it. My work focuses on leveraging environmental sequencing within phylogenetic frameworks to investigate the diversity, ecology, and evolution of microbial eukaryotes.

current.name: Bianca Sarcani
current.bio: I am a master student in Bioinformatics at Uppsala University. I am passionate about biodiversity, especially researching ways it can be accurately analysed and quantified using computational tools. I am developing an eDNA annotation pipeline to help identify fungal species in soil samples.

current.name: Linus Lassen
current.bio: I am a master student in Applied Biotechnology, fascinated by the planet's biodiversity. My thesis focuses on enhancing eDNA workflows to make biodiversity monitoring faster, more inclusive, and accessible. I am exploring portable sequencing with a single barcode marker to detect insects, protists, fungi, and plants from a single sample.

current.name: Caleb Caulk
current.bio: I am a master student in Data Science at Uppsala University. My thesis focuses on developing a pipeline that allows researchers to compare statistical and machine learning models on biodiversity predictions while allowing different configurations for intensive testing.

previous.name: Britt Andermann
previous.bio: I am a research librarian with a vested interest in the role natural history museum archives play in providing source material and biodiversity data for scientific research. I focus on highlighting archives as valuable entities from which to mobilize occurrence and taxonomic biodiversity data.

previous.name: Jiacheng Ling
previous.bio: I am an ecologist specializing in biodiversity and species distribution modeling. My interest focuses on geodiversity, spatial heterogeneity, and how it can help explain biodiversity patterns across habitats and taxa at local scales.

previous.name: Beilun Zhao
previous.bio: As an environmental biological researcher, my primary objective is to expand our understanding of spatial and temporal biodiversity to contribute to natural conservation efforts. My research focuses on the correlation between species ecological niches and environmental DNA across ecosystems.

previous.name: Filipe Almeida
previous.bio: I am a master student in the Erasmus Mundus Programme in Evolutionary Biology. My research interests lie in applying and developing computational methods for biodiversity conservation. I focus on predicting conservation status of fungal species in Sweden using machine learning.

previous.name: Alice Satre
previous.bio: I am a master student in life and environmental science. My interests are focused on forestry, ecology and biodiversity conservation. I joined the Biodiversity Data Lab as an intern to learn how to better understand and protect biodiversity.

previous.name: Shuangshuang Wang
previous.bio: As a forensic microbiological researcher, I work on the human microbiome and human DNA. Through this exchange opportunity, I explored environmental microbiology and environmental DNA to study distribution patterns of fungi in forests.

news.title: Schools engaged in forest biodiversity study
news.text: How does biodiversity differ between natural forests and production forests? Researchers Tobias Andermann and Mahwash Jamy from the Biodiversity Data Lab are seeking to find out with the help of school pupils throughout Sweden. The pupils will collect soil samples for analysis and sequencing at SciLifeLab.
